newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB tumbles as German deal terminated.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB tumbles as German deal terminated.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc fell in early trading on Friday after the company confirmed the collapse of talks with Germany's Kirch Gruppe to set up a German satellite television service.
The stock was down 22p at 601-1/2 by 0811 GMT.
In a statement following press reports that the deal had been terminated, BSkyB said the agreement had failed "because of failure to agree a number of fundamental issues."
Yet the stock recovered some of its initial drop and analysts pointed out that the failure was not a complete surprise.

"It had been going that way anyway," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "Really it is insignificant, the key thing for Sky is that the company has got huge momentum in its core business and any overseas expansion they can do on their own terms."
By 0836 GMT the stock was down just 12-1/2p at 611 in volume of 1.2 million shares.
